audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed as Job's reversal from former honor to present humiliation: mockers, social collapse, breached defenses, divine silence, bodily anguish, and failed expectation of good/light.

verses.restored: But now those younger than I laugh at me, whose fathers I would have refused to set with the dogs of my flock.

familiar.text: But now they that are younger than I have me in derision, whose fathers I would have disdained to have set with the dogs of my flock.

modern.text: “But now they mock me, men younger than I am, whose fathers I would have refused to entrust with my sheep dogs.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֤ה שָֽׂחֲק֣וּ עָלַי֮ צְעִירִ֥ים מִמֶּ֗נִּי לְיָ֫מִ֥ים אֲשֶׁר מָאַ֥סְתִּי אֲבוֹתָ֑ם לָ֝שִׁ֗ית עִם כַּלְבֵ֥י צֹאנִֽי

verses.restored: What use to me was the strength of their hands, men whose vigor had perished?

familiar.text: Yea, whereto might the strength of their hands profit me, in whom old age was perished?

modern.text: What use to me was the strength of their hands, since their vigor had left them?

original.text: גַּם כֹּ֣חַ יְ֭דֵיהֶם לָ֣מָּה לִּ֑י עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ אָ֣בַד כָּֽלַח

verses.restored: With want and hunger they are gaunt, gnawing the dry ground in gloom and desolation.

familiar.text: For want and famine they were solitary; fleeing into the wilderness in former time desolate and waste.

modern.text: Gaunt from poverty and hunger, they gnawed the dry land, and the desolate wasteland by night.

original.text: בְּחֶ֥סֶר וּבְכָפָ֗ן גַּ֫לְמ֥וּד הַֽעֹרְקִ֥ים צִיָּ֑ה אֶ֝֗מֶשׁ שׁוֹאָ֥ה וּמְשֹׁאָֽה

verses.restored: They pluck salt herbs by the bushes, and broom roots are their food.

familiar.text: Who cut up mallows by the bushes, and juniper roots for their meat.

modern.text: They plucked mallow among the shrubs, and the roots of the broom tree were their food.

original.text: הַקֹּטְפִ֣ים מַלּ֣וּחַ עֲלֵי שִׂ֑יחַ וְשֹׁ֖רֶשׁ רְתָמִ֣ים לַחְמָֽם

verses.restored: They are driven out from the midst; people shout after them as after a thief.

familiar.text: They were driven forth from among men, (they cried after them as after a thief;)

modern.text: They were banished from among men, shouted down like thieves,

original.text: מִן גֵּ֥ו יְגֹרָ֑שׁוּ יָרִ֥יעוּ עָ֝לֵ֗ימוֹ כַּגַּנָּֽב

verses.restored: They dwell in dreadful ravines, in holes of the dust and rocks.

familiar.text: To dwell in the cliffs of the valleys, in caves of the earth, and in the rocks.

modern.text: so that they lived on the slopes of the wadis, among the rocks and in holes in the ground.

original.text: בַּעֲר֣וּץ נְחָלִ֣ים לִשְׁכֹּ֑ן חֹרֵ֖י עָפָ֣ר וְכֵפִֽים

verses.restored: Among the bushes they bray; under nettles they huddle together.

familiar.text: Among the bushes they brayed; under the nettles they were gathered together.

modern.text: They cried out among the shrubs and huddled beneath the nettles.

original.text: בֵּין שִׂיחִ֥ים יִנְהָ֑קוּ תַּ֖חַת חָר֣וּל יְסֻפָּֽחוּ

verses.restored: Sons of fools, sons without name, they were whipped out of the land.

familiar.text: They were children of fools, yea, children of base men: they were viler than the earth.

modern.text: A senseless and nameless brood, they were driven off the land.

original.text: בְּֽנֵי נָ֭בָל גַּם בְּנֵ֣י בְלִי שֵׁ֑ם נִ֝כְּא֗וּ מִן הָאָֽרֶץ

verses.restored: And now I have become their song; I am a byword to them.

familiar.text: And now am I their song, yea, I am their byword.

modern.text: And now they mock me in song; I have become a byword among them.

original.text: וְ֭עַתָּה נְגִינָתָ֣ם הָיִ֑יתִי וָאֱהִ֖י לָהֶ֣ם לְמִלָּֽה

verses.restored: They abhor me; they keep far from me and do not withhold spit from my face.

familiar.text: They abhor me, they flee far from me, and spare not to spit in my face.

modern.text: They abhor me and keep far from me; they do not hesitate to spit in my face.

original.text: תִּֽ֭עֲבוּנִי רָ֣חֲקוּ מֶ֑נִּי וּ֝מִפָּנַ֗י לֹא חָ֥שְׂכוּ רֹֽק

verses.restored: Because he has loosened my cord and humbled me, they have cast off restraint before me.

familiar.text: Because he hath loosed my cord, and afflicted me, they have also let loose the bridle before me.

modern.text: Because God has unstrung my bow and afflicted me, they have cast off restraint in my presence.

original.text: כִּֽי יתרו פִ֭תַּח וַיְעַנֵּ֑נִי וְ֝רֶ֗סֶן מִפָּנַ֥י שִׁלֵּֽחוּ

verses.restored: On my right hand the rabble rises; they push away my feet and build up against me their roads of ruin.

familiar.text: Upon my right hand rise the youth; they push away my feet, and they raise up against me the ways of their destruction.

modern.text: The rabble arises at my right; they lay snares for my feet and build siege ramps against me.

original.text: עַל יָמִין֮ פִּרְחַ֪ח יָ֫ק֥וּמוּ רַגְלַ֥י שִׁלֵּ֑חוּ וַיָּסֹ֥לּוּ עָ֝לַ֗י אָרְח֥וֹת אֵידָֽם

verses.restored: They break up my path; they help my calamity; they need no helper.

familiar.text: They mar my path, they set forward my calamity, they have no helper.

modern.text: They tear up my path; they profit from my destruction, with no one to restrain them.

original.text: נָתְס֗וּ נְֽתִיבָ֫תִ֥י לְהַוָּתִ֥י יֹעִ֑ילוּ לֹ֖א עֹזֵ֣ר לָֽמוֹ

verses.restored: They come as through a wide breach; amid the crash they roll on.

familiar.text: They came upon me as a wide breaking in of waters: in the desolation they rolled themselves upon me.

modern.text: They advance as through a wide breach; through the ruins they keep rolling in. Job’s Prosperity Becomes Calamity

original.text: כְּפֶ֣רֶץ רָחָ֣ב יֶאֱתָ֑יוּ תַּ֥חַת שֹׁ֝אָ֗ה הִתְגַּלְגָּֽלוּ

verses.restored: Terrors are turned upon me; my dignity is chased like the wind, and my salvation passes like a cloud.

familiar.text: Terrors are turned upon me: they pursue my soul as the wind: and my welfare passeth away as a cloud.

modern.text: Terrors are turned loose against me; they drive away my dignity as by the wind, and my prosperity has passed like a cloud.

original.text: הָהְפַּ֥ךְ עָלַ֗י בַּלָּ֫ה֥וֹת תִּרְדֹּ֣ף כָּ֭רוּחַ נְדִבָתִ֑י וּ֝כְעָ֗ב עָבְרָ֥ה יְשֻׁעָתִֽי

verses.restored: Now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction seize me.

familiar.text: And now my soul is poured out upon me; the days of affliction have taken hold upon me.

modern.text: And now my soul is poured out within me; days of affliction grip me.

original.text: וְעַתָּ֗ה עָ֭לַי תִּשְׁתַּפֵּ֣ךְ נַפְשִׁ֑י יֹ֭אחֲז֣וּנִי יְמֵי עֹֽנִי

verses.restored: Night pierces my bones within me, and my gnawing pains do not lie down.

familiar.text: My bones are pierced in me in the night season: and my sinews take no rest.

modern.text: Night pierces my bones, and my gnawing pains never rest.

original.text: לַ֗יְלָה עֲ֭צָמַי נִקַּ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְ֝עֹרְקַ֗י לֹ֣א יִשְׁכָּבֽוּן

verses.restored: By great force my garment is disfigured; it binds me like the collar of my tunic.

familiar.text: By the great force of my disease is my garment changed: it bindeth me about as the collar of my coat.

modern.text: With great force He grasps my garment; He seizes me by the collar of my tunic.

original.text: בְּרָב כֹּ֭חַ יִתְחַפֵּ֣שׂ לְבוּשִׁ֑י כְּפִ֖י כֻתָּנְתִּ֣י יַֽאַזְרֵֽנִי

verses.restored: He has thrown me into the mire, and I have become like dust and ashes.

familiar.text: He hath cast me into the mire, and I am become like dust and ashes.

modern.text: He throws me into the mud, and I have become like dust and ashes.

original.text: הֹרָ֥נִי לַחֹ֑מֶר וָ֝אֶתְמַשֵּׁ֗ל כֶּעָפָ֥ר וָאֵֽפֶר

verses.restored: I cry to you, but you do not answer me; I stand, and you only look at me.

familiar.text: I cry unto thee, and thou dost not hear me: I stand up, and thou regardest me not.

modern.text: I cry out to You for help, but You do not answer; when I stand up, You merely look at me.

original.text: אֲשַׁוַּ֣ע אֵ֭לֶיךָ וְלֹ֣א תַעֲנֵ֑נִי עָ֝מַ֗דְתִּי וַתִּתְבֹּ֥נֶן בִּֽי

verses.restored: You have turned cruel to me; with the strength of your hand you oppose me.

familiar.text: Thou art become cruel to me: with thy strong hand thou opposest thyself against me.

modern.text: You have ruthlessly turned on me; You oppose me with Your strong hand.

original.text: תֵּהָפֵ֣ךְ לְאַכְזָ֣ר לִ֑י בְּעֹ֖צֶם יָדְךָ֣ תִשְׂטְמֵֽנִי

verses.restored: You lift me up to the wind; you make me ride it, and you dissolve me in the storm.

familiar.text: Thou liftest me up to the wind; thou causest me to ride upon it, and dissolvest my substance.

modern.text: You snatch me up into the wind and drive me before it; You toss me about in the storm.

original.text: תִּשָּׂאֵ֣נִי אֶל ר֭וּחַ תַּרְכִּיבֵ֑נִי וּ֝תְמֹגְגֵ֗נִי תשוה

verses.restored: For I know you will return me to death, to the house appointed for all living.

familiar.text: For I know that thou wilt bring me to death, and to the house appointed for all living.

modern.text: Yes, I know that You will bring me down to death, to the place appointed for all the living.

original.text: כִּֽי יָ֭דַעְתִּי מָ֣וֶת תְּשִׁיבֵ֑נִי וּבֵ֖ית מוֹעֵ֣ד לְכָל חָֽי

verses.restored: Yet does not one stretch out a hand in ruin, and in calamity cry out for help?

familiar.text: Howbeit he will not stretch out his hand to the grave, though they cry in his destruction.

modern.text: Yet no one stretches out his hand to a ruined man when he cries for help in his distress.

original.text: אַ֣ךְ לֹא בְ֭עִי יִשְׁלַח יָ֑ד אִם בְּ֝פִיד֗וֹ לָהֶ֥ן שֽׁוּעַ

verses.restored: Did I not weep for the one whose day was hard? Was not my soul grieved for the needy?

familiar.text: Did not I weep for him that was in trouble? was not my soul grieved for the poor?

modern.text: Have I not wept for those in trouble? Has my soul not grieved for the needy?

original.text: אִם לֹ֣א בָ֭כִיתִי לִקְשֵׁה י֑וֹם עָֽגְמָ֥ה נַ֝פְשִׁ֗י לָאֶבְיֽוֹן

verses.restored: But when I hoped for good, harm came; when I waited for light, darkness came.

familiar.text: When I looked for good, then evil came unto me: and when I waited for light, there came darkness.

modern.text: But when I hoped for good, evil came; when I looked for light, darkness fell.

original.text: כִּ֤י ט֣וֹב קִ֭וִּיתִי וַיָּ֣בֹא רָ֑ע וַֽאֲיַחֲלָ֥ה לְ֝א֗וֹר וַיָּ֥בֹא אֹֽפֶל

verses.restored: My inward parts boil and do not rest; days of affliction confront me.

familiar.text: My bowels boiled, and rested not: the days of affliction prevented me.

modern.text: I am churning within and cannot rest; days of affliction confront me.

original.text: מֵעַ֖י רֻתְּח֥וּ וְלֹא דָ֗מּוּ קִדְּמֻ֥נִי יְמֵי עֹֽנִי

verses.restored: I walk darkened, but not by the sun; I stand in the assembly and cry for help.

familiar.text: I went mourning without the sun: I stood up, and I cried in the congregation.

modern.text: I go about blackened, but not by the sun. I stand up in the assembly and cry for help.

original.text: קֹדֵ֣ר הִ֭לַּכְתִּי בְּלֹ֣א חַמָּ֑ה קַ֖מְתִּי בַקָּהָ֣ל אֲשַׁוֵּֽעַ

verses.restored: I have become a brother to jackals and a companion to daughters of the ostrich.

familiar.text: I am a brother to dragons, and a companion to owls.

modern.text: I have become a brother of jackals, a companion of ostriches.

original.text: אָ֭ח הָיִ֣יתִי לְתַנִּ֑ים וְ֝רֵ֗עַ לִבְנ֥וֹת יַעֲנָֽה

verses.restored: My skin turns black and falls from me, and my bones burn with heat.

familiar.text: My skin is black upon me, and my bones are burned with heat.

modern.text: My skin grows black and peels, and my bones burn with fever.

original.text: ע֭וֹרִי שָׁחַ֣ר מֵעָלָ֑י וְעַצְמִי חָ֝֗רָה מִנִּי חֹֽרֶב

verses.restored: My lyre has become mourning, and my flute the voice of weepers.

familiar.text: My harp also is turned to mourning, and my organ into the voice of them that weep.

modern.text: My harp is tuned to mourning and my flute to the sound of weeping.

original.text: וַיְהִ֣י לְ֭אֵבֶל כִּנֹּרִ֑י וְ֝עֻגָבִ֗י לְק֣וֹל בֹּכִֽים
